title: Code review report: T-002 Packages 2 and 3 (T-002f to T-002l) and Package 1 review fixes
summary: Round 1 for Packages 2 and 3, and a re-review of the Package 1 fixes: APPROVE. There are no blockers or major issues and 9 minor ones. The flaky test_many_simultaneous_reviews_exactly_one_wins was a test-harness bug, not an application bug, and the reviewer fixed the test: 30 of 30 runs of the test and 30 of 30 runs of the whole concurrency module now pass. Optimistic concurrency, the append-only audit trail, authorisation on every new route, PATCH and review validation, and conflict handling that keeps typed text are sound. Package 1: the MAJOR (contrast on the surface) and 5 of 7 minors are fixed. The two-round validation and fastapi 0.162.2 are still open. Backend 737 passed (1 environment skip), Vitest 101 + 200 passed, Playwright e2e 127 passed. Screenshots were re-captured with the Operative wording.

items.label: Symptom.
items.text: About 1 failure in 10 runs before the fix. The failure was never in the race itself: the warm-up GET .../history returned 500 in one thread, which aborted the barrier for the other 7 (BrokenBarrierError).

items.label: Cause (test problem).
items.text: Each thread builds its own app, and FastAPI builds route state lazily on the first requests. While doing so it wraps a pydantic TypeAdapter in warnings.catch_warnings() to silence UnsupportedFieldAttributeWarning. In Python 3.13 catch_warnings swaps the process-wide filter list and is not thread-safe, so one thread leaving it restores the filters while another thread is still inside. pytest's filterwarnings = error then raises the warning, which surfaces as a 500. With 8 threads the overlap is likely; with 2 it is rare. Production is not affected: warnings are not errors there, and uvicorn builds routes on the single event-loop thread. Row locking and version checks were never involved.

items.label: Fix (backend/tests/test_concurrency.py).
items.text: A module-level _SETUP_LOCK serialises each thread's login and warm-up. The warm-up now also builds the review and PATCH routes, using an unknown id so they return 404 and write nothing. The barrier and the requests under test still run concurrently. Verified: the test passed 30 of 30 runs, the whole concurrency module 30 of 30, and ruff, ruff format and the full backend suite are clean (737 passed). Owner: tests (already done by the reviewer, so nothing to do).

items.label: Tests.
items.text: pytest: 737 passed, 1 skipped (sandbox network check). Vitest: shared 101 passed, web 200 passed (2 opt-in screenshot skips). Playwright e2e with system Chrome against the dev stack: 127 passed, 6 skipped (screenshot spec without SCREENSHOT_DIR).

items.label: Live API probes (dev backend).
items.text: PATCH: {}, version-only, version as '1', true or 1.0, notes as an int, 5,001 characters, NUL, a lone surrogate, photos, review_status, checklist null or [], a bad uuid, a foreign id, label, done null or 'yes', duplicate ids, an empty item, an array body, text/plain and deeply nested JSON all return 422 with the right loc. Two problems give two entries. Review: {}, 0, -1, 1.5, '1', true, an extra key and null return 422. A huge version returns 409 (no crash). Admin and painter get 403 and anonymous 401 on PATCH, review and report history. Manager and painter get 403 and anonymous 401 on /admin/settings/history. PUT, DELETE, PATCH and POST on history return 405.

items.label: Database.
items.text: On the dev database, UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE of audit_events and TRUNCATE job_reports CASCADE all fail with 'audit_events is append-only'. Both triggers are enabled.

items.label: Screenshots.
items.text: Re-captured with SCREENSHOT_DIR=reports/screenshots (6 passed). The reviewer inspected login (360px), dashboard (768 and 360px), report detail and awaiting (360 and 768px) and report edit (768 and 360px). 'Operative' wording, review panel, history panel and edit form all render without horizontal overflow. These are the queue layout issues listed above.

Concurrency: review and edit both start with session.get(..., with_for_update=True) on a fresh per-request session, so READ COMMITTED returns the committed row after the lock. The version compare comes after the lock, there is one commit, and any ProblemError rolls back and releases the lock. A no-op edit rolls back explicitly. Review against edit is serialised on the same row lock (test_a_review_racing_an_edit_one_wins). Reopen happens in the same transaction with one version bump, records reopened after edited, and a racing double reopen yields exactly one reopened event. Checklist items are only changed under the report lock. The order of checks matches the spec: 404, then foreign item 422, then 409, then diff.

Audit: record_event is called inside each write service before the single commit, so a failed write leaves no event (409 and 422 tests check event counts). Settings no-ops record nothing. actor_name is a snapshot. request_id comes from a validated header pattern. request_id and old_id are stored but _to_schema returns only field, item_id, item_label, old_value and new_value. History is manager or admin only, and manager_notes appear only on manager endpoints. Triggers apply to the owner too. Only the seed loader sets the truncate setting, and the seed refuses to run outside local and test.

Authorisation: the new routes sit on the router-level require_roles guards (manager and admin). The access loop is generated from the contract and now covers PATCH and POST with a body, so authorisation wins over validation.

Validation: extra keys are forbidden at every level. version is a strict int >= 1. done is a strict bool and an explicit null is rejected. Notes reject NUL and lone surrogates and count code points. A blank note becomes null in the service only, so validation messages refer to the raw input.

Frontend conflicts: EditReportForm pins the report it started from (useState(report)), so a background refetch never moves the version forward. On 409 the typed values stay in the form, and 'Current saved value' is shown only for fields that were sent. A retry whose 409 names the current user with current values equal to the body is treated as saved, so there is no duplicate event. 403 keeps the text. Unsaved-changes protection uses both useBlocker and beforeunload. QueryBoundary keeps children mounted on a background error, so the form is not lost.

XSS: notes, history before and after values, item labels and names are rendered only as JSX text (pre-wrap). There is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML in web/src or shared/src. The e2e checks that markup in notes is shown literally and that 1,200 characters fit at 360px.

T-002l: WORDING is the one source of the trade words, and roleLabel uses it. The API, generated client and contract are unchanged. A wording test guards the chrome. The only remaining trade words in the UI are job-type labels (T-002m, out of scope) and identifiers.
Should the 17 remaining x-ticket markers in api/openapi.yaml be removed now that PENDING_TICKETS is empty, or are they kept as provenance?
